title: Ganzhou Kingdom
capsule: The Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom was a Turkic dynastic state established along the Hexi Corridor in present-day Gansu by the Yaglakar clan, survivors of the Uyghur Khaganate's collapse in 840. Centered at Ganzhou (modern Zhangye), it controlled a strategic stretch of the Silk Road and maintained diplomatic relations with the Song dynasty. The kingdom came under increasing pressure from the Tangut Xi Xia state and was finally absorbed by Xi Xia around 1036, ending Uyghur political sovereignty in the region for centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the kingdom's core along the Hexi Corridor is clear but outer boundaries are reconstructed from fragmentary Chinese dynastic records and archaeological inference.
